s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive neurological decline with cerebellar and brainstem involvement
salient_findings: Morning headaches with nausea and vomiting
Numbness, tingling, and weakness in upper extremities
Blurred or double vision, vertigo, and clumsy gait
Vertical and horizontal nystagmus and gait ataxia
key_facts: 2-month history of progressively worsening symptoms
No significant past medical history
Headaches did not fully resolve with analgesics
Numbness, tingling, and weakness in both upper extremities
Intermittent blurred or double vision, vertigo, and clumsy gait
Vertical and horizontal nystagmus on neurologic examination
Gait ataxia on neurologic examination
Cranial nerve function otherwise normal
Mass lesion centered in the fourth ventricle region on head CT
Surrounding brain edema and obstructive hydrocephalus on head CT
Well-demarcated, relatively homogeneous mass on T2-weighted brain MRI
Mass filling the fourth ventricle, causing cerebellar compression and tonsillar herniation

shortlist.label: Medulloblastoma
shortlist.why_kept: Location in the fourth ventricle and symptoms of cerebellar and brainstem involvement

shortlist.label: Ependymoma
shortlist.why_kept: Common location in the fourth ventricle and potential for causing obstructive hydrocephalus

shortlist.label: Pilocytic astrocytoma
shortlist.why_kept: Common in young adults, can occur in the cerebellum, and may cause symptoms of increased intracranial pressure

shortlist.label: Subependymoma
shortlist.why_kept: Typically occurs in the fourth ventricle and can cause obstructive hydrocephalus, matching the patient's symptoms

shortlist.label: Choroid plexus papilloma
shortlist.why_kept: Can occur in the fourth ventricle, may cause hydrocephalus, and is a consideration in young adults with cerebellar symptoms

raw.rationale: The tumor's location in the fourth ventricle and its well-demarcated, homogeneous appearance on MRI are consistent with ependymoma, which often arises from the ependymal lining of the ventricles and can cause obstructive hydrocephalus and cerebellar compression.

rejected.label: Medulloblastoma
rejected.why: Typically more heterogeneous and located in the cerebellum

rejected.label: Pilocytic astrocytoma
rejected.why: Often has a cystic component and is more commonly found in the cerebellum

rejected.label: Subependymoma
rejected.why: Usually found in the lateral ventricles and has a more irregular appearance

rejected.label: Choroid plexus papilloma
rejected.why: Typically found in the lateral ventricles and has a more cauliflower-like appearance
